waypoints.name: Rainy Pass Trailhead (SR 20)
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass required; parking is at the Rainy Pass picnic area, trailhead sign at the north end of the lot.
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) to Rainy Pass near milepost 157.5, about 50 miles east of Marblemount or 35 miles west of Winthrop, and turn into the Rainy Pass Picnic Area on the south side of the highway; the Lake Ann/Maple Pass trailhead sign is at the north end of the lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The highway closes for the winter over the pass.

waypoints.name: Heather Pass junction
waypoints.note: Leave the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Loop trail #740 here onto the unmaintained climbers' path toward Lewis and Wing Lakes.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail #740 about 1.3 miles through forest to the signed fork, stay right toward Heather Pass (the left fork goes to Lake Ann), and climb through meadows to Heather Pass, where you leave the maintained trail for the unmarked climbers' path toward Lewis and Wing Lakes.

waypoints.name: Talus field crossings
waypoints.note: Two loose talus fields to cross on the climbers' path before Lewis Lake; cairned but easy to lose in fog.
waypoints.directions: Follow the unmarked, cairned climbers' path west from Heather Pass across two loose talus and boulder fields. The cairns are easy to lose in fog or under early-season snow, and this is the main route-finding problem of the approach.

waypoints.name: Lewis Lake
waypoints.note: Lower, less-established camp option; only a couple of decent tent spots on the north shore.
waypoints.directions: Beyond the second talus field, drop down to Lewis Lake. The few tent sites are in the timber on the north shore.

waypoints.name: Wing Lake outlet
waypoints.note: Reliable water; the lake outlet is the last dependable source before the summit push.
waypoints.directions: From Lewis Lake, climb about 1,200 ft of meadow and talus west to Wing Lake.

waypoints.name: Wing Lake camp
waypoints.note: Standard base camp for Black Peak climbers; best established tent sites are here rather than Lewis Lake.
waypoints.directions: The established tent sites are in the trees on the right (north) as you reach the lake.

waypoints.name: South col
waypoints.note: Gained from Wing Lake by going around its north side, then up a moraine and permanent snowfield; a broad gully on the west side leads to the summit blocks.
waypoints.directions: Go around the right (north) side of Wing Lake, climb the moraine and permanent snowfield into the obvious talus and snow gully below the col, and angle climber's right out of it near the top to avoid the cliff bands directly below the col.

waypoints.name: Black Peak summit
waypoints.note: Class 3 with easy class 4 moves near the top; helmet recommended for rockfall off the summit block.
waypoints.directions: From the col, scramble north along the cairned south ridge toward the summit pyramid; a short class 4 step of about 15 ft guards the top.

evidence.measurement: USGS GNIS 1516618 'Black Peak' summit point, DomesticNames_WA
USGS 3DEP: highest cell of a 9x9 grid (11 m spacing) round the GNIS point is 16 m away (8,979 ft)

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek Trailhead (Colonial Creek Campground)
waypoints.note: Overnight stays need a North Cascades backcountry permit, reserved on Recreation.gov or picked up at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount; the trail starts at the south end of Colonial Creek Campground near the boat ramp off SR 20.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR 20, the North Cascades Highway, to Colonial Creek Campground near milepost 130 on Diablo Lake. The Thunder Creek trail starts at the south end of the campground, near the boat ramp, at about 1,200 ft. Overnight stays in the park need a North Cascades backcountry permit.

waypoints.name: Junction Camp
waypoints.note: Established hiker/stock camp about 10 miles in; cross a log bridge to the creekside hiker camp with views of Boston Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Thunder Creek Trail south along Thunder Arm and up the Thunder Creek valley, past McAllister and Tricouni camps, about 10 miles to Junction Camp at the Fisher Creek Trail junction. The last mile or so below the camp is a steep climb.

waypoints.name: Park Creek Pass
waypoints.note: Broad, flat, rocky trough at Thunder Creek's headwaters; leave the maintained trail here and head east into the moraine toward the Fremont Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Stay on the Thunder Creek Trail rather than turning onto the Fisher Creek Trail, and continue up the upper Thunder Creek valley past Thunder Basin to Park Creek Pass, a broad, rocky trough at about 6,000 ft at the head of the creek.

waypoints.name: Point 8248 / Fremont Glacier saddle camp
waypoints.note: Rock-outcrop bivy sites at the southern margin of the Fremont Glacier with nearby running water; standard high camp for the summit push.
waypoints.directions: Leave the maintained trail at the pass and climb east about 500 ft into the moraine, then traverse north around a broad ridge over heather and rock for roughly 1.5 to 2 miles, crossing a rib near 7,600 ft and a gully through cliff bands that can hold snow or ice, to the bivy sites on the saddle at the southern edge of the Fremont Glacier.

waypoints.name: Fremont Glacier hogsback and bergschrund
waypoints.note: Rope up for glacier travel; the snow hogback at the upper edge of the glacier can leave a bergschrund exposed in late season.
waypoints.directions: Rope up and make the gentle glacier crossing north from camp to the Hogsback, the snow spine at the upper edge of the Fremont Glacier. Late in the season a bergschrund and a moat can open where the snow meets the rock.

waypoints.name: Western ramp / U-notch summit ridge gain
waypoints.note: A Class 3-4 rock pitch gains a left-slanting ramp (a fault-line weakness) to the summit ridge, then exposed Class 2-3 ledges lead through a U-notch between the summit tower and south horn.
waypoints.directions: Cross the moat onto rock and climb a Class 3-4 pitch to a left-slanting ramp, a fault-line weakness in the cliff bands, which leads up to the summit ridge. Do not head straight at the summit tower from the glacier.

waypoints.name: Mount Logan Summit
waypoints.note: Tiny summit gained via a final Class 3-4 rock pitch; reverse via the same route with a short rappel off the summit block.
waypoints.directions: Traverse exposed Class 2-3 ledges on the east side of the ridge through the U-notch between the summit tower and the south horn, then climb a final Class 3-4 pitch of about 100 ft on solid rock to the tiny summit.

road.name: Icicle Road, Eightmile Road (FR 7600) and FR 7601 to the Stuart Lake Trailhead
road.status: Steep gravel that gets washboarded as the season goes on; a high-clearance vehicle is advised, with four-wheel drive if you have it. Vehicles are barred from FR 7601 each winter.
road.driveNote: Leave Leavenworth on Icicle Road and go roughly 8.5 mi to the Eightmile Road (FR 7600) turnoff on the left. Bear right onto FR 7601, pass the Eightmile Trailhead, and carry on about 4 mi to the road end at about 3,400 ft. Space is tight: once the lot fills, use only the side of the road the signs allow, since parking in the marked zones is ticketed.
road.seasonalGate: FR 7601 is closed to vehicles every winter.

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: The Stuart Lake Trailhead is at the end of Forest Road 7601, reached from Icicle Road out of Leavenworth by way of Eightmile Road (FR 7600); the lot sits at about 3,400 ft. Overnight stays in the Colchuck Zone need a quota wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake
waypoints.directions: Follow the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 about 2.5 miles to the signed fork where the Colchuck Lake Trail #1599.1 splits left and south. Continue roughly 1.8 miles more, crossing Mountaineer Creek and a boulder-hop stretch near the outlet, to the lake at 5,570 ft. This is the last easy, reliable water, so fill here because there is none above.

waypoints.name: Aasgard Pass
waypoints.directions: Skirt the lake's south and east shoreline on a braided, cairned climbers' path over talus and slab to the foot of the obvious steep gully and headwall at the head of the lake. Aasgard gains roughly 2,000 ft in under a mile on dirt switchbacks, loose scree and boulder-hopping; cairns get knocked over and the path splits into several use trails, so keep re-picking the line toward the notch. Firm snow and ice can linger into July, making an axe and sometimes crampons worthwhile on what is otherwise a scramble.

waypoints.name: Core Enchantments
waypoints.directions: From the pass, cross the grey talus and glacial till of the upper Core Zone past Tranquil Lake (Lake Freya) and Isolation Lake, then drop slightly into the meadow-and-tarn complex sometimes called the Brisingamen Lakelets.

waypoints.name: Base of north slopes
waypoints.directions: Near the far end of the meadows, watch for an unsigned climbers' path forking right, to the west, toward Little Annapurna. If you cross a stream and pass a toilet sign you have gone by the junction and should backtrack.

waypoints.name: Little Annapurna summit
waypoints.directions: Above here it is a scatter of cairned, well-worn boot paths rather than a trail. Take the line of least resistance up the broad north-facing slabs and talus on the peak's east side, switchbacking and scrambling at low 3rd class at most. The true summit is the middle of three rocky high points along the crest.

USGS 3DEP: highest cell of a 9x9 grid round the GNIS point is 40 m away (8,475 ft); OSM peak node 356548164 is 24 m away

road.name: SR 970, North Fork Teanaway Road and FR 9737 to the Esmeralda Trailhead
road.status: Paved state highway and county road, then gravel Forest Road 9737 to its end.
road.driveNote: Head out of Cle Elum on SR 970 for roughly 8.5 mi, then go left on the North Fork Teanaway Road for 13 mi. Bear right on FR 9737 and drive about 9.6 mi to the road-end lot at 4,269 ft. Space is limited: keep the road clear for emergency vehicles, and if the lot is full the only roadside parking allowed is on the west side.
road.seasonalGate: Check road status with the Cle Elum Ranger District before an early- or late-season trip.

waypoints.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead (N Fork Teanaway River Rd)
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Fork Teanaway River Road (FS-9737) to its end at the Esmeralda Basin / Longs Pass trailhead, about 4,300 ft. The road is usually open to the trailhead by early June, but the route itself wants late June through September, once the Longs Pass approach and the rock are snow-free. From the lot take the Longs Pass Trail (#1229), which climbs roughly 2.3 miles and 2,300 ft to Longs Pass.

waypoints.name: Long's Pass
waypoints.directions: From the lot, follow the Esmeralda Basin trail 0.3 mile and turn right onto the Ingalls Way Trail (#1390). Climb about 1.4 miles to the junction at about 5,440 ft, turn right onto the Longs Pass trail, and switchback steeply up open, rocky slopes about 1.2 miles to the pass.

waypoints.name: Sherpa south basin camp
waypoints.directions: Drop steeply off the north side of the pass on the boot path, about 1,400 ft, to Ingalls Creek; ford or rock-hop it and follow the Ingalls Creek Trail east about a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike junction. Leave the trail on the climbers' path up through timber and brush, climb the rib staying left of its crest, and at about 5,800 ft traverse right over the rib into the basin below Sherpa.

waypoints.name: Base of west ridge
waypoints.directions: Climb class 2 snow and talus up the basin past the flat table-rock shelf at about 7,400 ft to the notch at the west foot of the ridge, on the col between Stuart and Sherpa; aim for the notch closest to Sherpa.

waypoints.name: Sherpa Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb blocky class 4 ridge trending climber's left to a cave belay, then take the crack out of the cave (the crux, about 5.4 to 5.5). Continue left to a platform with a rappel anchor, scramble across a short gully, climb to the lowest point of the summit ridge, and follow it on exposed class 4 to the summit block.

evidence.measurement: USGS GNIS 1531559 'Sherpa Peak' summit point, DomesticNames_WA
USGS 3DEP: highest cell of a 9x9 grid round the GNIS point is 16 m away (8,611 ft); OSM peak node 348973980 is 37 m away

waypoints.name: Beverly Turnpike Trailhead (#1391)
waypoints.note: South/Teanaway-side approach via Beverly Creek and Fourth Creek trails toward Ingalls Creek, then bushwhack/scramble up to the SE side of the peak. Matches this route's own recorded GPS track almost exactly.
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 85 east of Cle Elum, follow SR 970 about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Keep right onto North Fork Teanaway Road, which becomes gravel FR 9737 at 29 Pines Campground. Continue just under 4 miles and, just before the Beverly Creek bridge, turn right onto FR 9737-112, a rough one-lane spur best with high clearance, for about 1.4 miles to its end at about 3,650 ft.

waypoints.name: East end of ridge
waypoints.directions: Take Beverly Turnpike Trail #1391 up Beverly Creek, bearing left at about 0.5 mile rather than onto the Bean Creek trail. At about 3.1 miles turn right onto Fourth Creek Trail #1226.1, cross Fourth Creek Pass (about 6,000 ft), and descend to Ingalls Creek at about 6 miles and ford it. Leave the Ingalls Creek Trail and climb north into the Porcupine Creek basin, working up beside the southeast ridge to its foot.

waypoints.name: Argonaut Peak summit (true/west summit)
waypoints.directions: Climb about eight pitches up the crest of the southeast ridge, blocky and lichen-covered low down, to the southeast spire. Make two single-rope rappels or one double-rope rappel into the notch beyond, then continue to the true summit on the west spire.
